title: Hiroshima Marks 81st Bombing Anniversary as Takaichi Hedges on Non-Nuclear Principles, Protesters Rally
detail: Roughly 50,000 people gathered at Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park on August 6, 2026 for the 81st anniversary ceremony marking the US atomic bombing that killed an estimated 140,000 people. Hiroshima's mayor criticized major powers for justifying possession of nuclear weapons as deterrence. Prime Minister Takaichi, attending, said she would pursue a 'realistic approach' to nuclear disarmament within the Non-Proliferation Treaty framework but avoided a clear pledge to uphold Japan's Three Non-Nuclear Principles (not possessing, producing, or permitting the introduction of nuclear weapons) — a departure in wording from past premiers, consistent with her prior writing that the 'no introduction' principle is unrealistic. The same day, protesters rallied in Hiroshima and Osaka against the Takaichi government's security agenda, including the new National Intelligence Bureau and relaxed lethal-arms export rules, urging the government to confront Japan's wartime history.

media.caption: Hiroshima marks the 81st anniversary of the atomic bombing
